subject: Deployment mode discussion — Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@finsecure.com>

Cc: Mike Johnson <mike.johnson@finsecure.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Deployment mode discussion — Dedicated vs Private VPC

Hi Marissa / team,

Thanks again for taking time to meet today. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can move toward procurement: 

- Our core requirement is strong data isolation for customer PII and payment data (PCI scope). We are a regulated finance app — SOC2 is a baseline requirement.
- Primary question: would Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) meet our needs, or do we need Private VPC / on-prem/offline deployment to satisfy our security/compliance team?
- Requirements / constraints:
  - Bring-your-own-key (AWS KMS) support is mandatory.
  - Audit logs for at least 12 months.
  - Data-at-rest + in-transit encryption, and the ability to limit network egress so data doesn’t leave our VPC.
  - Retention policy: 30 days prefered, but we can discuss options.
  - Latency SLO target: ~200ms per inference (95th).
  - Expected load: low-to-moderate — ~1k requests/day, 800–1k tokens per request on average.

Next steps for us: please send a short doc that explains the differences in data isolation between Dedicated and Private VPC (including where data persists, how KMS is integrated, and audit/log access), a ballpark cost range, and a draft SOW we can share with procurement.

Thanks — looping in Mike from procurement on the CC.

Best,
Sarah Kim
Head of Product Security, FinSecure Capital

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Deployment mode discussion — Dedicated vs Private VPC

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear recap. Appreciate the detail; below is a concise explanation and a couple of follow-ups so we can put a draft SOW together quickly. Attached: Redwood_Dedicated_Datasheet.pdf, SOC2_summary.pdf.

Short answer: Dedicated capacity will meet many data-isolation requirements, but Private VPC / Private deployment is recommended when your compliance team requires customer-controlled networking or avoidance of any shared hardware tenancy. Details: 

- Redwood Hosted API: multi-tenant hosted endpoints. Fastest to deploy, but not suitable when BYOK or strict tenancy isolation is required.

- Redwood Dedicated (recommended if you want managed service + stronger isolation):
  - Reserved GPU pool logically dedicated to your account (tenant-level isolation).
  - Network isolation options: VPC peering / private ingress so traffic flows from your VPC into our dedicated pool; customer traffic does not traverse public IPs.
  - BYOK: we support AWS KMS integration for key management; customer keys never leave your control.
  - Data persistence: model inputs/outputs are encrypted at rest; we can offer configurable retention policies (30 days default for this engagement).
  - Audit logs: centralized logging with per-request traces and exportable audit logs (we can retain >=12 months as requested, additional retention is an add-on).
  - Hardware tenancy: Dedicated is logical (tenant-dedicated) — if your compliance requires physical single-tenant hardware or no shared kernels, consider Private.

- Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem):
  - Full customer-managed VPC and optional on-prem package. Control plane can be customer-hosted in your VPC; no shared tenancy.
  - For customers that must avoid any shared hardware or require air-gapped deployments, this is the path.

Clarifying questions (short):
1) Data classification: you mentioned PCI and PII — is PHI in scope at all?
2) KMS: are you planning to use AWS KMS (we support that) or an HSM vendor?
3) Retention: is 30 days non-negotiable, or can this be adjusted per dataset?
4) Throughput/latency: the 200ms SLO is achievable with appropriate model sizing and Dedicated throughput sizing — can we confirm target p95 and expected concurrency?

Proposed next steps:
- I’ve attached a one-page Dedicated datasheet and our SOC2 summary.
- I’ll loop in Aditya (Solutions Engineering) and Dylan (Infra Solutions) for a technical deep dive to validate the network/KMS integration and to size Dedicated capacity.
- If it looks like you need Private, we’ll include an outline of the additional steps (control plane placement, network setup, and procurement for on-prem if required).

Available times for a 45-minute technical call next week:
- Tue Mar 3, 10:00–10:45 PT
- Wed Mar 4, 14:00–14:45 PT
- Thu Mar 5, 09:00–09:45 PT

Please let me know which works and answer the clarifying Qs above so we can prepare a draft SOW.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@finsecure.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment mode discussion — Dedicated vs Private VPC

Marissa / team — thanks, that’s helpful. Quick answers below and a few follow-ups so the SOW can reflect our constraints: 

- Data classification: no PHI. We are in PCI and PII scope.
- KMS: AWS KMS (we want BYOK).
- Retention: 30 days is our standard for inference logs; can discuss exceptions for audit artifacts.
- Audit logs: 12 months mandatory.
- Latency: p95 under 200ms is the target.
- Load: roughly 1k requests/day, concurrency low (<5 concurrent requests typical), ~800–1k tokens per request.
- Hardware tenancy: our compliance team’s preferred stance is to avoid multi-tenant hardware when PCI is in scope, but they are open to a documented risk assessment if Dedicated provides strong network isolation and BYOK.
- Procurement window: aiming to complete procurement in ~6 weeks.

Ask: can you include a short section in the SOW that describes the physical/virtual tenancy model for Dedicated (i.e., whether GPUs are co-located with other customers on the same host) and any mitigations you provide for side-channel risks? Also please include a ballpark committed monthly cost for the Dedicated pool sized to our throughput so procurement has a number to budget.

Thanks — can do Tue Mar 3 at 10:00 PT for the technical call.

Best,
Sarah
